outcome.technical: tools/reach-diff.py, the five review findings. R9: the hook is written as usercustomize, which site imports after whichever sitecustomize won. hook_entry() asks the interpreter once, under the sweep's ambient_env, whether its user site is on, and falls back to writing a sitecustomize only when it is off; the output's `hook:` line says which and what the fallback costs. The hook installs once per process (sys._reach_diff_hooked) and chains to the module of its own name that it shadows. Each process writes `<token>.start` at install and `<token>.json` at exit, carrying its parent's token (handed down in REACH_DIFF_PARENT), whether it runs the module (sys.argv[0] resolves to it), and how many subprocess.Popen children it started with the module's path among their arguments (sys.addaudithook). read_traces() counts started, written and silent processes, and untraced_children(): per writing process, the module children it spawned less the module processes that wrote naming it as parent. RULE, stated in the docstring: a revision with any untraced module child, or an unreadable trace file, refuses with 2. R10 and R11: line_keys and its occurrence index are replaced by match_lines() in three passes: difflib.SequenceMatcher per function present at both, then over the rest of the module in line order, then by text alone. A base-reached line paired with an unreached head line is lost (exit 1) and named under the function it is in now. Only a line whose text the head holds nowhere is gone, and gone does not decide the exit. R12: the CONTRIBUTING.md bullet now says 'in every Python process that imports its hook', alignment by text, a line moved into another function still judged, gone only when the text is nowhere and not failing, and the untraced-child refusal. R13: the docstring's THE ROUTE IS THE SWEEP'S section states the effect. The usercustomize entry removes it, since no sitecustomize is added; the sitecustomize fallback keeps it, and both the docstring and the `hook:` line say so. A dict of reason strings (HOOK_NOTES) failed gate-parity's ea1/ea4-ea7 as an unclassified reason table and became the function hook_line(). Selftest 22/22: new rd17 to rd22, rd10 and rd11 rewritten for match_lines, rd1 to rd9 and rd12 to rd16 unchanged and passing. The same 22/22 under /usr/bin/python3 3.9, where every process used settrace. The hook source extracted alone passes `vermin -t=3.8-`, minimum 3.8. ruff exit 0. Sweep runs: tools/reach-diff.py 22 cases, tests/test__output_lints.py 182 cases, tools/gate-parity.py 119 cases (`3/3 files ok, 323 cases`, exit 0); test__deps (266), test__areas (130), test__refs (292), test_derive_phase_gate (36) (`4/4 files ok, 724 cases`, exit 0); tools/_suite.py, tools/affected.py and tools/check-committed-pii.py green in the run before the hook_line fix. REAL RUN: `python3 tools/reach-diff.py plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py tests/test_drive_phase.py --base 92c399f5 --head HEAD`, HEAD = bc1169a8, exit 1, real 228.37 s (user 564.10 s, sys 837.42 s), 8 jobs, measured once; the previous run took 716.9 s. hook: usercustomize. Base: 5808 lines, 125 blocks, 685 processes started the hook and 681 wrote, 0 module children untraced. Head: 5784 lines, 77 blocks, 600 started and 596 wrote, 0 untraced. Lost: the same 35 lines in 13 functions as the previous run, among them the advance sign-off route (triage 7564-7569, drive_locked 9295-9299). PINNED/WINDOWS CHILDREN NOW TRACED, measured on the one block bc-block at HEAD (_brief_crlf_cases, which runs _windows_stdout), via scratchpad/one_block.py. Entry usercustomize: started 5, written 5, untraced 0, 1524 lines. Entry sitecustomize (the landed design): started 11, written 11, untraced 1, 1517 lines. So the old entry left that child untraced and the count now catches it, and the process count shows the route effect R13 named.
outcome.descriptive: reach-diff now traces children behind a suite's own sitecustomize and refuses with 2 when a module child it counted never wrote. It finds a line moved to another function, or hidden behind an identical inserted line. The drive-suite comparison takes 228 s instead of 717 s.

testsAdded: rd17: a module child started under a non-chaining sitecustomize planted ahead of the hook is traced, so dropping it exits 1 naming its lines. rd18: a child handed an environment without the hook counts as untraced, exit 2. rd22: a child that ends through os._exit after reaching the module counts as untraced, exit 2. rd21: the hook adds no sitecustomize to PYTHONPATH and a fully traced run counts nothing untraced; this is the over-fire direction. rd19: a line moved into a new function and left unreached exits 1 under that function, not gone. rd20: an identical line inserted earlier in the same function does not hide the later copy's loss, exit 1 naming it. rd10 and rd11 rewritten: alignment pairs each old copy with itself, and a moved line is paired with its new number.
claims:
claims:
1 'written as usercustomize ... falls back to sitecustomize' = hook_entry() and write_hook(directory, entry); 'installs once per process' = the sys._reach_diff_hooked guard in HOOK_SOURCE; 'counts the children it starts through subprocess.Popen with the module's path' = on_event and names_module in HOOK_SOURCE; 'refuses with 2' = the `blind` branch in _judge; three-pass matching = match_lines(); 'gone ... does not decide' = _judge sets code from found["gaps"] only. Each CONTRIBUTING sentence maps to one of these.
2 Landed logic in a throwaway copy: 14/20, rd17 to rd22 red. Mutation probe after the fix: entry-always-site -> rd17 rd21 red; untraced-never -> rd18 rd22 red; untraced-always (over-fire) -> 13 red; no-text-rematch -> rd19 red; by-occurrence -> rd10 rd20 red; restored 22/22. The once-per-process guard has no case that observes it: with a single entry module it cannot fire twice, and I say so here rather than claim it is tested.
3 The class is lines or processes silently out of the measurement. `grep -n 'continue\|except' tools/reach-diff.py`: each silent-skip site was reviewed. read_traces' unreadable files now decide the exit (2) and are no longer only printed. A `.part` file is skipped by design, and is visible as started minus written. reach_gaps skips a reached line that is not a code line, which a line event cannot produce. The landed `processes traced` count, which could not tell untraced from converted, is replaced by started, written and untraced.
4 The CONTRIBUTING rule still says in its own sentence that nothing runs the tool automatically (no verify.sh slice, no hook) and that it runs where a task names it in its gate.
5 Real-run wall 228.37 s is measured once and labelled so. Lines reached are identical across three runs on different days and hooks (5808 and 5784 in the first run, the separate HEAD-only trace and this run). The bc-block comparison was run once per entry.
6 n/a - no guard. The untraced rule reads what the processes did (spawn events against written traces), not command text.
7 No number in the docstring or CONTRIBUTING prose; the figures here sit beside the commands that produced them.
